newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen schoolyard gunman to be shot, crucified.
newsitem.headline: Yemen schoolyard gunman to be shot, crucified.

text.p: A Yemeni appeals court on Wednesday upheld a death sentence against a Yemeni man for killing four children and two adults in an attack at two schools and said he should be executed and his body crucified for three days in a Sanaa street.
"We order that the accused be executed by firing squad and crucified for three days...to be a deterrent to others," the three-judge panel told a packed courtroom.

It said Mohammad Ahmad Misleh, 48, should be executed in the street where the two schools he attacked are located. Misleh on Sunday opened fire from an assault rifle on hundreds of schoolchildren in the courtyards of the adjacent schools as the students lined up for morning classes.
He killed a headmistress, a teacher and four children.
The ruling still has to be ratified by Yemen's supreme court and President Ali Abdullah Saleh. Legal sources said the procedure was a formality.
